learningObjectives: Scan a PDF file with the PDF Engine 3.0 and create text, image, and table controls.
Explain why anchor controls are needed and state the three conditions a valid anchor must meet.
Configure anchor accuracy when an exact match causes identification problems.
Compare a reference PDF against target files using the PDF 1:1 Compare Module.

elements.description: The PDF Scan defines document regions for testing. Unlike HTML scanning, this workflow selects text, image or table areas in the document. Start Scan → PDF from a Module folder or use Ctrl+Shift+P, choose a file, then inspect the selected content before saving the Module.

elements.title: Two reasons to scan a PDF
items: To test the text, images, or tables the PDF contains.
To mark areas that should be EXCLUDED from a PDF comparison — for example a timestamp or an invoice number that legitimately changes on every run.

elements.title: Three control types
items: Image control — verifies a visual element.
Table control — checks tabular data, with configurable row and column headers.

elements.text: Use Content Preview to check text and table recognition, including spaces. Force optical recognition is an alternative when the extracted content is wrong; choose the document language for OCR. Scanning an exclusion region alone does not configure a comparison.

bulletPoints: Scanning is not only for verification — the exclusion use case is what makes comparison of dynamic documents practical.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Anchor controls: the core concept of this lesson

elements.description: A target may move when document content changes. Absolute coordinates can still be used for fixed layouts. Use an anchor when the target retains a stable position relative to a distinctive element on the same page.

At runtime the engine finds the anchor, then calculates the target region from its recorded offset. Both may move together; if the distance between them changes, anchor identification alone does not guarantee the correct target.

elements.title: Three conditions a valid anchor must meet
items: It must be a text or image element.
It must be uniquely identifiable — not part of a repetitive area.
It must be on the same page as the target control.

elements.text: Repeated labels can make an anchor ambiguous. Inspect its uniqueness after redraw or rescan; the scan highlights ambiguous anchors in orange. Select a distinctive same-page landmark.

bulletPoints: Anchor = a stable landmark. Target = found relative to that landmark.
Text or image · unique · same page — all three, or it is not a valid anchor.

elements.description: The dedicated Tosca 2026.1 anchor configuration page specifies 100% matching accuracy for text anchors and 99% for image anchors. The scan overview describes exact matching more generally; use the type-specific guidance when configuring the Module.

For a problematic anchor, select its ModuleAttribute and add the transition parameter Accuracy in the Properties pane. Use an integer from 0 to 100. This setting controls anchor matching; it is different from the comparison Module’s Accuracy [%] and from forcing OCR during scanning.

elements.text: Treat lowered accuracy as a targeted fix for a specific problematic anchor, not as a default to apply everywhere. A too-forgiving match can silently anchor to the wrong element and produce a test that passes against the wrong region of the document.

bulletPoints: Text anchor default: 100%; image anchor default: 99%. Adjust the Accuracy transition parameter for a specific anchor only after investigating the mismatch.

elements.description: PDF 1:1 Compare compares a reference PDF with one or more targets using a configured minimum similarity, Accuracy [%]. Page by Page Image is the default. Full Text Content ignores text position and does not support OCR text recognition; Page by Page Text compares corresponding pages. Choose the mode that matches the assertion.

elements.text: Current location: Standard modules → Engines → Pdf → PDF 1:1 Compare. Do not infer the Module inventory or shortened names of an inaccessible older course subset from the current documentation.

elements.description: Scan the variable region, save the Module, and use Copy Dimensions on its ModuleAttribute. In the comparison TestStep, populate the excluded area’s Dimensions and Page(s). This explicitly connects the scanned region to the exclusion; verify that the chosen region does not hide meaningful defects.

elements.text: Excluded Pages and Excluded Text provide additional targeted exclusions; text patterns can be literal or regex. For link checks, the Standard subset includes Check PDF for Broken Links and Extract Links; link extraction does not require scanning.
📄 Official Tricentis Academy exercise material for this lesson is not redistributed here — complete the exercises inside the official course.

bulletPoints: Select a comparison type and a minimum similarity threshold; compare the intended reference and targets.
Configure exclusion dimensions and pages explicitly; simply scanning a region does not exclude it.

examPitfalls.title: Choosing an anchor that is not unique
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Anchoring to a column header, page footer, or label that appears more than once in the document.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use a distinct text or image on the same page. Repeated content can be ambiguous; check uniqueness after rescanning or redrawing.

examPitfalls.title: Anchoring to an element on a different page
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using a distinctive heading from page 1 as the anchor for a value on page 3 because it is the most unique text in the document.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The anchor must be on the same page as the target control. Uniqueness alone is not sufficient; find a same-page landmark even if it is less distinctive.

examPitfalls.title: Lowering anchor accuracy as a default habit
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reducing accuracy across all anchors to avoid identification failures.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Investigate recognition and uniqueness first. Text anchors default to 100%, image anchors to 99%; lower a specific anchor’s Accuracy transition parameter only when justified, and confirm that it still locates the intended region.

examPitfalls.title: Comparing dynamic PDFs without excluding volatile regions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Running PDF 1:1 Compare against a document containing a generation timestamp and treating the resulting failure as a real defect.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Scan the variable region and copy its dimensions into the comparison’s excluded area with the appropriate pages. Inspect exclusions so they cannot conceal meaningful changes.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting the anchor to be a table or arbitrary region
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Trying to anchor to a table control or a blank area of the page.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: An anchor control must be a text or image element. Table controls exist for verifying tabular data, not for serving as anchors.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When is anchor-based identification preferable to absolute PDF coordinates?

options.text: Because PDFs cannot be scanned at all.
When the target moves but retains a stable offset from a unique same-page text or image.
Because anchors make the TestCase run faster.
Because Tosca cannot read text from PDF files.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what happens to a value's coordinates when a table above it gains a row.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An anchor supports relative positioning when the anchor and target retain their relationship. Fixed coordinates remain useful for fixed layouts; an anchor cannot compensate for an arbitrary change in the offset.

optionExplanations.A: PDF Scan can create document controls; inability to scan is not the reason for relative identification.
optionExplanations.B: A stable offset from a uniquely identifiable same-page anchor supports a target that moves with it.
optionExplanations.C: Anchor use addresses identification; it does not establish a universal execution speed advantage.
optionExplanations.D: Text controls and OCR recognition are supported; text extraction is not categorically unavailable.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which conditions must an anchor control satisfy? (three correct answers)

options.text: It must be a text or image element.
It must be uniquely identifiable and not part of a repetitive area.
It must be on the same page as the target control.
It must be positioned above the target control.

practiceQuiz.hint: Three rules: what it can be, how distinctive it must be, and where it must live.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A valid anchor must be text or image, uniquely identifiable rather than part of a repetitive area, and on the same page as the target. There is no requirement about the direction of the anchor relative to the target — it can sit above, below, or beside it.

optionExplanations.A: Text and image controls are valid anchor types; tables are not.
optionExplanations.B: A unique anchor avoids ambiguous matching; repetitive areas cannot serve as anchors.
optionExplanations.C: The anchor must be on the target’s page so its relative location can be used.
optionExplanations.D: Being above the target is not a requirement; the relative position must instead remain stable.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which three control types can be created when scanning a PDF?

options.text: Text, Image, and Table
Text, Link, and Button
Header, Body, and Footer
Field, Form, and Signature

practiceQuiz.hint: One for words, one for pictures, one for structured data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The PDF Scan creates Text controls for textual content, Image controls for visual elements, and Table controls for tabular data with configurable row and column headers.

optionExplanations.A: These are the three PDF Scan control categories.
optionExplanations.B: Link verification uses dedicated Modules; Link and Button are not the three scan categories.
optionExplanations.C: These describe document regions, not the supported scan control types.
optionExplanations.D: These are possible document features, not the scan’s Text, Image and Table categories.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A generated invoice PDF must be compared against a reference file, but it contains a generation timestamp that differs on every run. What is the correct approach?

options.text: Lower the PDF 1:1 Compare accuracy until the test passes.
Scan the timestamp region, copy its dimensions into the comparison’s excluded area, set its pages, then compare.
Compare only the first page.
PDFs with dynamic content cannot be compared.

practiceQuiz.hint: Excluding areas from a comparison is one of the two stated purposes of the PDF Scan.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Configure the excluded area’s Dimensions and Page(s) using the scan result. This removes the intended variable region while retaining checks elsewhere; merely creating a scanned control does not set the comparison exclusion.

optionExplanations.A: Reducing the global threshold can conceal unrelated differences rather than excluding the known variable region.
optionExplanations.B: Dimensions and page scope explicitly connect the scanned timestamp area to the comparison exclusion.
optionExplanations.C: The timestamp may remain on page one, and dropping later pages discards other checks.
optionExplanations.D: Targeted area, text and page exclusions allow comparison of PDFs containing dynamic content.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What determines the PDF 1:1 Compare result when using its default comparison type?

options.text: The files must be byte-for-byte identical.
It compares page images against the configured minimum similarity, Accuracy [%].
It only compares the text layer and ignores images.
It always requires manual confirmation.

practiceQuiz.hint: The threshold is configurable rather than absolute.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The default mode is Page by Page Image. Accuracy [%] specifies the minimum similarity; other modes compare text, so visual comparison is not the only supported configuration.

optionExplanations.A: This is a configured content comparison, not a byte-level file identity requirement.
optionExplanations.B: Page by Page Image is the default; the configured minimum similarity determines its comparison result.
optionExplanations.C: Text-only modes exist, but the default mode compares images of corresponding pages.
optionExplanations.D: The Module supplies an automated comparison result; manual approval is not its pass criterion.

quickRecap.value: Right-click a Module folder → Scan, or Ctrl+Shift+P.
Test text/images/tables, or exclude areas from a comparison.
Relative identification works when the target retains its offset from a unique same-page text or image.
Text or image · uniquely identifiable · same page as the target.
Text: 100%; image: 99% by default. Configure the anchor ModuleAttribute’s Accuracy transition parameter (0–100).
Default: Page by Page Image; optional text modes. Accuracy [%] sets minimum similarity; exclusions require explicit TestStep configuration.
